name: Riz · Strength, size & sub-40 10k
why: Hybrid block: 4 lifting days (Upper/Lower × strength and volume) plus 2 quality runs. Upper/Lower lets each muscle be trained twice a week, the frequency research supports for hypertrophy, while keeping the heavy lower-body day away from the interval run to limit interference between strength and endurance training. Strength days use 4–6 reps at 2 reps in reserve (high mechanical tension, low fatigue); volume days use 8–15 reps for extra hypertrophy stimulus. Weekly sets: chest ~14, back ~13, quads ~11, hamstrings ~9, shoulders ~8 side/rear plus pressing, which sits in the productive range for an intermediate lifter, with legs kept moderate because running adds lower-body fatigue. Double progression (reps through the range, then +2.5 kg upper / +5 kg lower) with effort ramping up over the block and a week-8 deload. Running: one VO2max interval session (1 km reps starting at your current 5k pace, about 4:15/km, speeding up to 4:00/km) and one long easy run, the two sessions with the biggest pay-off for a 10k when running only twice a week. Session order Mon–Sat: Upper Strength, Lower Strength, Upper Volume, Intervals, Lower Volume, Long run, so the hard run never follows heavy squats.
note: Tempo = seconds down · pause · up · pause. Keep the rest times on main lifts. Order matters: intervals sit 48 h after heavy squats. If you feel fresh, add an optional 30-min easy run on Sunday from week 3. Week 8: deload plus a 5k time trial to set next block's paces.

exercises.name: Barbell bench press
exercises.note: Main lift. Builds to 100 kg × 4 by week 7
exercises.why: Highest-load horizontal press: heavy loads build the strength (and confidence) you need for 100 kg. The 1-second pause on the chest removes the stretch-reflex bounce so the pecs and triceps do the work, and matches competition-style control. 3 min rest keeps quality high on every set.

exercises.name: Pull-up
exercises.note: Add weight with a belt once you hit 8 on all sets
exercises.why: Vertical pull with the lats loaded through a full range from a long, stretched position. Balances the pressing volume and builds the upper back that stabilises a heavy bench.

exercises.name: Overhead press
exercises.why: Front delts and triceps carry over directly to bench lockout; standing also trains trunk stiffness. Kept at 3 sets to manage shoulder fatigue alongside bench volume.

exercises.name: Chest-supported row
exercises.note: Chest on an incline bench, pause at the top
exercises.why: Chest support removes lower-back fatigue (you squat and RDL tomorrow and run on Saturday), giving a better stimulus-to-fatigue ratio than barbell rows. The pause at the top targets mid-traps and rhomboids, which keep the shoulder blades set on the bench.

exercises.name: Close-grip bench press
exercises.note: Hands just inside shoulder width
exercises.why: A narrower grip shifts load towards the triceps, the usual sticking point near lockout. Two sets keep it as targeted accessory work rather than extra chest fatigue.

exercises.name: Face pull
exercises.note: Pull towards your eyes, thumbs back. Superset with hammer curls
exercises.why: Rear delts and external rotators: balances all the pressing and keeps the shoulders healthy under heavy loads. A low-fatigue, high-rep exercise, so it can be taken close to failure.

exercises.name: Hammer curl
exercises.note: Superset with face pulls
exercises.why: Brachialis and brachioradialis add arm thickness; brings direct biceps work to 5 sets a week for your hypertrophy goal without lengthening the session (superset).

exercises.name: Back squat
exercises.note: Main lift. Builds to 122.5 kg × 4 by week 7
exercises.why: Most loadable lower-body lift: quads, glutes and adductors under high mechanical tension. The controlled 3-second descent and pause build strength out of the hole without needing near-maximal loads, and placing it two days before the interval run gives the legs time to recover.

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
exercises.note: Hips back, bar close, stop at the hamstring stretch
exercises.why: Trains the hamstrings and glutes at long muscle lengths, where research shows strong hypertrophy, with less spinal and recovery cost than conventional deadlifts. Strong hamstrings also support running mechanics.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
exercises.note: Reps per leg
exercises.why: Single-leg strength and stability that carries over to running stride, and fixes left/right imbalances. Only 2 sets, because it's very fatiguing.

exercises.name: Standing calf raise
exercises.note: 2-second pause in the stretch at the bottom
exercises.why: Calves and Achilles take the most load when running. Pausing in the stretched position increases hypertrophy and tendon stiffness, which helps running economy and protects against Achilles problems.

exercises.name: Hanging leg raise
exercises.note: No swinging
exercises.why: Trunk flexion with the hip flexors: a stiffer trunk transfers force better under the bar and when running.

exercises.name: Barbell bench press
exercises.note: Volume day: same lift, lighter, more reps
exercises.why: Practising the main lift twice a week improves skill (motor learning) and adds chest hypertrophy volume at a load that doesn't affect Monday's heavy day.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell press
exercises.note: Bench at about 30°
exercises.why: Upper chest (clavicular head) and a deeper stretch than a barbell allows. Dumbbells let each arm move along its own path, easing shoulder stress.

exercises.name: Lat pulldown
exercises.why: Vertical pull at moderate reps; easier to progress in small steps than pull-ups for volume work.

exercises.name: Seated cable row
exercises.note: Let the shoulder blades travel forward on each rep
exercises.why: Horizontal pull with constant cable tension and a full stretch at the front of each rep: upper back thickness to support the bench.

exercises.name: Cable fly
exercises.note: Pause in the stretch
exercises.why: Cables keep tension at the stretched position, where the pecs grow well, with very little triceps or shoulder fatigue.

exercises.name: Cable lateral raise
exercises.note: Cable from behind you, lead with the elbow
exercises.why: Side delts are only lightly worked by pressing; direct work builds shoulder width. A cable keeps tension at the bottom, where dumbbells offer none.

exercises.name: Overhead cable extension
exercises.note: Superset with curls to save time
exercises.why: Overhead puts the triceps long head at full stretch, which research shows grows more than pushdowns. The long head is two-thirds of arm size and drives lockout.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell curl
exercises.why: Arms behind the body stretch the biceps long head, the position that gives the most hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Easy jog warm-up
exercises.note: Then 4 × 20 s strides
exercises.why: Raises muscle temperature and primes the nervous system so the first rep is at target pace, not a shock.

exercises.name: 1 km interval
exercises.note: Start at 4:15/km (about your current 5k pace). Every 2 weeks: one more rep, and 5 s/km quicker if the last rep felt controlled (aim 4:00/km by week 7). 90 s easy jog between
exercises.why: VO2max intervals work best at roughly current 5k pace. Starting at 4:15/km (not goal pace) keeps every rep repeatable; pace and reps rise together towards 4:00/km, your sub-40 race pace.

exercises.name: Easy jog cool-down
exercises.why: Clears fatigue and adds easy aerobic volume at almost no recovery cost.

exercises.name: Leg press
exercises.note: Moderate: you run long tomorrow
exercises.why: Quad volume with almost no spinal or balance demand, so plenty of stimulus for little fatigue the day before the long run.

exercises.name: Hip thrust
exercises.note: Squeeze hard at the top
exercises.why: Glutes are loaded hardest at full hip extension, the same position you drive through when sprinting and running uphill.

exercises.name: Seated leg curl
exercises.why: Seated puts the hamstrings at a longer length than lying curls, and research shows more hypertrophy from it. It complements the RDL by training knee flexion.

exercises.name: Leg extension
exercises.note: Pause at the top
exercises.why: Isolates the rectus femoris and the quads near full knee extension, the part of the range squats underload. Low fatigue.

exercises.name: Seated calf raise
exercises.why: Bent-knee calf raises target the soleus, the main calf muscle for running endurance.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.note: Squeeze glutes and abs
exercises.why: Anti-extension core endurance, which holds your posture late in a run when fatigue sets in.

exercises.name: Easy long run
exercises.note: 5:00–5:20/km, conversational. From week 3, run the last 10 min at 4:30/km (current 10k pace), 4:20/km from week 5
exercises.why: Easy running builds mitochondria, capillaries and fat use at little recovery cost: the aerobic engine a 10k depends on. It adds 5 min a week up to 75 min.

exercises.name: Strides
exercises.note: Fast but relaxed, walk back between
exercises.why: Short fast efforts improve running mechanics and economy without adding fatigue.
